gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-todhr: Industrial, with wide porthole counters, Existence traces each letter in one steady line of constant weight. But where Existence excels at crisp, unbroken outlines, Noto Serif Todhri wins on sturdy curves and a sizable x-height.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-yezid: Noto Serif Yezidi forms solid blocks of words rather than skylines. Existence traces each wide-countered letter in one steady thickness, while the classic serif lets heavier verticals tug against lighter horizontals.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-pt-serif-caption: Industrial, bent from one length of tubing, Existence holds its porthole counters wide. And PT Serif Caption comes in with a tall x-height and hairlines close to its stems, so the two hold together on the page.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-judson: Strong and clean, Franchise draws every letter with a single nib, tall and tightly packed. But Judson, the classic serif, does contrast best, with stencil-bold stems against fine hairlines.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-rashi-hebre: Bookish and quietly engraved, Noto Rashi Hebrew keeps a soft, tilted-nib variation in every stroke. And Franchise is the one to follow with a finger, its outline tall, tight and constant in width.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Pipe-like strokes, tightly packed: that's Franchise. Noto Serif Ahom, a text serif, swells gently on its curves and stands lofty in the lowercase, so it can stay modest in size.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-balin: Glass tubing bent into tall, tightly packed letters: that is Franchise. Noto Serif Balinese tapers only slightly and stands tall in the lowercase, so it holds its own against that tube-bent heading.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-devan: Strong and clean, Franchise holds one pen width throughout, with tall small letters jammed close. And Noto Serif Devanagari reads literary and unhurried, its slimmer curve tops and short ascenders keeping a big lowercase gentle over paragraphs.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-dives: Noto Serif Dives Akuru is refined, with soft contrast in every curve. Franchise is best at uppercase built from lines of one constant thickness, while the serif gives short-looking capitals and moderately weighty stems.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-georg: Authoritative, Noto Serif Georgian carries a slight bulge on its bowls while Franchise stays tall, tight and free of calligraphic swelling. Its subdued contrast across the alphabet rewards a slightly generous size.
